page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor. The configuration allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz, paired with 128 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Hardware caches include 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Vector extensions are restricted to standard AVX, lacking AVX-512 or AMX support, while standard cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are available.

The instance does not include local disk storage, requiring external cloud storage volumes for persistent data. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default. Acceleration hardware is absent, with no GPUs attached to the instance.

Benchmark data displays strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng evaluations, reaching the upper 25th percentile, alongside competitive lightweight text generation speeds for small language models. However, broader multi-core metrics, including Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU scores, fall into the median range. Evaluated memory bandwidth indicates an architectural tradeoff: while small cached blocks sustain over 1000 GB/sec, large uncached transfers drop into the lower quartile at 35.69 GB/sec read and 17.06 GB/sec write throughput.

Given its substantial memory capacity and 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU density balanced against moderate network capacity and uncached memory speeds, the ecs.r7a.4xlarge is suited for in-memory caching solutions like Redis, relational database management systems, batch ETL processing, and enterprise application servers requiring large RAM footprints without high local disk I/O requirements.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor clocked at 2.55 GHz, paired with 128 GB of RAM. The x86_64 architecture incorporates standard AVX, AES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, but excludes AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Built without local storage or GPU hardware, the instance relies on external block storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU execution, while multi-core compute, general processing scores, and Redis operations remain average. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the lower quartile, contrasting with strong cached throughput. With an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation, ecs.r7a.4xlarge is tailored for in-memory databases, backend caching layers, mid-scale enterprise applications, and memory-dependent data processing workflows.
